System

Death, shrine respawn and reconnect policy

Death replaces the combat body state without wiping progression. A safe shrine/bind point provides recovery; a client reconnect is not allowed to reset inventory, undo a death penalty or refresh all resources for free.

Scope and player interaction

Death replaces the combat body state without wiping progression. A safe shrine/bind point provides recovery; a client reconnect is not allowed to reset inventory, undo a death penalty or refresh all resources for free.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase08committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Alive → Defeated → PenaltyPending → RespawnAvailable → Respawning → Ready → RecoveryError

WBP_Death observes results from URPGRecoveryComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Recovery_Default. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
DeathId: unique character/session/body-life identifier
BindPointId: unlocked safe entrance or shrine; persisted
DurabilityPenaltyPercent=0.05; configurable and rounded under one rule
Persistent facts retained: XP, quest progress, inventory, equipped identities, currencies
Transient policy: cancel casts/gather/fish/trade preparation, clear short harmful statuses
RespawnResourcePolicy: full health, 50% mana/stamina proposal; long cooldowns preserved
CombatLogoutGraceSeconds=15 proposal; server body remains vulnerable during grace

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGRecoveryComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_DeathLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
HandleDefeat(DeathId) -> PendingPenalty|AlreadyProcessed; server
CommitDeathPenalty(CommandId, DeathId) -> Applied|AlreadyApplied; backend economic command
RequestRespawn(DeathId, BindPointId) -> Spawned|Pending|InvalidBindPoint
RecoverAfterDisconnect(CharacterId, Epoch) -> DurableAliveState|DeathRecovery|TransferRecovery

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Authoritative health reaches zero once; recovery owner marks dead, cancels actions and notifies encounter/group systems.
  2. Backend command applies configured durability/currency policy at most once. No inventory destruction or XP rollback is allowed by the default.
  3. WBP_Death observes death/penalty readiness and shows a clear respawn option; it never resets attributes directly.
  4. Server verifies a safe unlocked bind point and spawns/repossesses one replacement body; PlayerState ASC rebinds to that avatar.
  5. Restore persistent inventory/quests/XP unchanged, apply respawn resource/status policy and retain selected long cooldown expiry records.
  6. A disconnected live body follows combat grace and checkpoint rules. Rejoining restores the committed alive/dead state; it cannot choose an old local save to avoid death.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Place Shrine_Hearthford outside enemy/resource collision and register its SpawnPointId in DA_Zone_Rillmere. Add a kill-floor recovery fallback per zone.
  2. Create DA_Recovery_Default and WBP_Death; the Respawn button calls the controller's validated recovery request, then waits for possession/readiness.
  3. Reopen GAS initialization to distinguish initial login, new body after death and cross-zone reconstruction. Do not regrant starting items or duplicate abilities on each respawn.
  4. Reopen gathering/fishing/dialogue/trade components to cancel transient work by matching action/offer ID; committed results remain durable.
  5. Place Hazard_Test in a marked lab-only corner, not on the production PlayerStart. Run lethal and simultaneous-disconnect scenarios with Client_B observing.

Reopen Phase08 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / Shrine_Hearthford / Hazard_Test. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Repeated death callback -> one DeathId/penalty.
Disconnect after penalty committed but before respawn -> reconnect still dead/respawn-ready, no second penalty.
Bind point missing or map unavailable -> validated zone safe-hub fallback, not arbitrary client coordinates.
Inventory full at death -> no item loss; durability changes affect equipped instances only.
Old pawn sends late RPC -> WrongAvatar/SessionFenced; new body unaffected.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Default penalty is 5% equipped durability loss, no currency subtraction; repairs create the modest economic cost. Proposed respawn delay 5 seconds. These can be tuned but must not become a rollback mechanic.

Record DeathId, penalty receipt and body-life identifier. Death UI is keyboard/controller accessible, has text instructions and no required rapid reaction.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
